# `start_export_image`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start an asynchronous copy or move of saved images from one storage volume to another.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd5ad0, StartExportImage @0x130190 (64-bit build) |

Enumerates the selected files and directories synchronously, checks that source and destination differ and that both storages are mounted, copies the selection and options into global state, resets the success counter and starts the export worker. A success reply means the worker was started. The worker copies the selected files and accessories; with keep false it may remove each source after copying. It reports progress through ExportImage events (fields state, lapse, total, keep, dst_storage; state values start, frame_complete and complete; the counters count files or frames, and complete is also sent after a requested stop, so it does not prove every copy succeeded). The final counts are returned by stop_export_image. No camera or mount gate, request timeout or rollback exists; enumeration and locks can block.

Side effects: Starts a worker thread that copies (and with keep false, deletes) image files between storage volumes; resets export counters; broadcasts ExportImage progress events.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_export_image"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional parameters of start_export_image. A single-element array [object] is also accepted; absent, null, scalar and empty-array params behave as an empty object. An unknown key, or a files member that is not an array, is rejected with 109. Duplicate keys are processed in order, and file selections resolve against the source in force at that point, so a later src does not rebase earlier selections. [READ] |
| `params.keep` | boolean | no | true | Keep source files after copying. false permits the worker to delete sources. A boolean or integer is accepted (zero false, non-zero true); a failed conversion silently leaves the current value. [READ] |
| `params.src` | string | no | the current storage | Source storage name (emmc, sd or udisk), matched case-insensitively and exactly; unknown names map to an invalid storage. The handler reads the member without a type check, so a non-string has no safe canonical reply. [READ] |
| `params.dst` | string | no | the current destination setting | Destination storage name; same matching as src. Must differ from src. [READ] |
| `params.files` | array<string> | no | - | Entries under the source image path to export. Each string selects a path: an existing regular file adds the file and its accessories, a directory enumerates its media and adds a directory marker, a missing path is skipped. Non-string entries are skipped. When files is omitted the whole source image path is enumerated. An empty or all-invalid selection is rejected with 267. No path sanitisation or bounds are shown. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 109 | Unknown params key, or files is not an array | `unexpected param` |
| 267 | The selected list is empty after enumeration | `no image` |
| 209 | Source and destination storage are the same | `invalid value` |
| 318 | Source or destination storage is not mounted | `device not connected` |
| 204 | Unknown storage id when its image path is requested (the mounted check may give 318 first) | `out of limit` |
| 268 | An export is already running | `operation is in progress` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A thread-start failure is forwarded with its own code. A malformed src or dst has no established type-error code and can be unsafe.

## Example

Request, default-copy:

```json
{"id":111,"method":"start_export_image","params":{"keep":true}}
```

Request, move-selected:

```json
{"id":112,"method":"start_export_image","params":{"src":"emmc","dst":"udisk","keep":false,"files":["Example_target"]}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_export_image","result":0,"code":0,"id":111}
```

Reply, same-storage:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_export_image","error":"invalid value","code":209,"id":113}
```
